findings.explanation: In kube-apiserver a webhook call failure, including a timeout, is recorded with error_type=calling_webhook_error (only when failurePolicy is Fail); apiserver_internal_error is reserved for other internal errors. The UC's 'apiserver gave up waiting' signal therefore points at the wrong label value.
findings.quote: apiserver_admission_webhook_rejection_count with error_type apiserver_internal_error indicates the apiserver gave up waiting, which is distinct from policy denial rejections
findings.suggested_fix: Describe timeouts as error_type="calling_webhook_error" on apiserver_admission_webhook_rejection_count (fail-closed hooks), and apiserver_admission_webhook_fail_open_count for failurePolicy=Ignore hooks; keep apiserver_internal_error only as a separate internal-fault signal. Apply the same correction in dataSources.

findings.explanation: Application State is deprecated since CIM 4.12.0 and models host process/service/port inventory; it has no app, info or state fields and nothing in kube-apiserver webhook histograms maps to it or to Performance. The implementation and dataModelAcceleration text ('accelerate CIM Application_State and Performance for cluster entities') repeats the same misfit.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the CIM models (the detection is raw Prometheus metrics with no CIM mapping) or state plainly that no CIM datamodel applies; remove the acceleration instructions from implementation and dataModelAcceleration.

findings.explanation: description states a 'greater than zero' paging rule and an Application_State source, but the SPL reads raw Prometheus metrics and tiers severity on p99_ms versus the per-hook budget, frac_wall_pct (20/35/45%), shed_rpm (2/5/20) and internal_rej >= 3.
findings.quote: from datamodel `Application_State`. Rolls up `calls_5m`, `cum_at_le`, `p50_le` by `cluster`, `hook_name`, `hook_type`, `op` across `5m` and pages when `wh_cnt` > 0, `histo_total` > 0, `step_cnt` > 0, or `hook_avg_ms` > 0
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the real logic: per cluster, webhook, type and operation in 5-minute windows, flag hooks whose P99 approaches or exceeds the p99_budget_ms from k8s_webhook_latency_budget.csv, whose share of apiserver request time exceeds 20/35/45%, or that coincide with 429/504 shedding.

findings.explanation: dataSources (and app, plus the trailing detailedImplementation Step 1 'Enable the modular input ... poll interval 300–900 seconds') describe a forwarder modular input, while the rest of the UC and the Kubernetes guide describe the Splunk OTel Collector prometheus receiver sending to HEC at 15–60 s scrape intervals.
findings.quote: Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
findings.suggested_fix: State a single collection path: Splunk OpenTelemetry Collector for Kubernetes prometheus receiver scraping kube-apiserver /metrics, exported over HEC to k8s_metrics. Remove the Universal Forwarder and modular-input wording.

findings.explanation: After the UC-specific Steps 1-5 and closing checklist, a second generic Step 1-5 block is appended that contradicts them (earliest=-24h@h vs -30m@m, 300–900 s polling vs 15–60 s scrapes, comparing counts to a 'vendor admin UI inventory', checking HTTP 401/429 'from the vendor endpoint').
findings.quote:
Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the trailing generic Step 1–5 block so only the webhook-specific procedure remains.

findings.explanation: The entries are templated and name no real cause of a slow-webhook alert; the genuine benign causes are already listed in detailedImplementation (policy-engine cold cache after upgrade, GitOps apply storms, managed control-plane maintenance windows).
findings.quote: Batch `sum` on `prometheus:scrape:metrics`** — Scheduled automation elevates `hook_name` without crossing `wh_cnt` > 0
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with concrete causes: Kyverno/Gatekeeper cache warm-up for one or two windows after an upgrade, GitOps or Helm mass-apply storms that multiply admission calls, provider control-plane maintenance, and deliberate load tests; say how to recognise each (change record, single-bucket spike, apply-controller user agent).

findings.explanation: The SPL fails at parse time (non-streaming commands inside multisearch) and joins on CIM fields that do not exist, so it cannot have been run end to end; the reviewer field is a generic repository handle, not an SME.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft or community until the search has been executed against real kube-apiserver metrics and signed off by a named reviewer.

findings.explanation: kube-apiserver sets the type label to "admit" for mutating webhooks and "validating" for validating webhooks; there is no "mutating" value. The same text calls 429 and 504 'verbs' when they are HTTP codes.
findings.quote: apiserver_admission_webhook_request_total (operation, name, type mutating or validating)
findings.suggested_fix: Write "type (admit for mutating webhooks, validating for validating webhooks)" and "filtered to code 429 and 504".

findings.explanation: The SPL closing table projects 18 columns (cluster through cim_app_state); the closing checklist repeats 'sixteen'.
findings.quote: The closing table lists sixteen analyst columns.
findings.suggested_fix: Say eighteen columns, or drop the column count.

findings.explanation: The Splunk OTel Collector for Kubernetes is a Helm chart (Splunkbase 6790 per the guide), not a Splunk add-on; the linked 'Add-on for Kubernetes' page could not be confirmed and appears to document a different product, if it exists.
findings.quote: Splunk OpenTelemetry Collector for Kubernetes ([Splunk Add-on for Kubernetes documentation](https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/AddOns/released/Kubernetes/About))
findings.suggested_fix: Check that the docs.splunk.com URL resolves; if not, link the splunk-otel-collector-chart GitHub repo or Splunkbase 6790 and drop the add-on label (also in references).

findings.explanation: kube-state-metrics does not expose apiserver admission metrics, and the sig-auth folder and controller-runtime manager.go links are not about the signals used here.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with the kube-apiserver admission metrics source or metrics reference entries and the ValidatingWebhookConfiguration timeoutSeconds/failurePolicy docs.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: multisearch only accepts purely streaming subsearches, but every arm contains stats (and the histogram arm also sort 0 and eventstats). Splunk fails with 'Multisearch subsearches may only contain purely streaming operations'. Restructure: one base search with the metric-name filter, then a single stats, or use append.

_total, _sum, _count and _bucket series are cumulative Prometheus counters, yet the SPL takes sum(mv) or max(mv) of raw samples per 5-minute bucket. calls_5m and shed_rpm become sums of counter readings (not per-window or per-minute counts), hook_avg_ms and frac_wall_pct become lifetime-since-restart ratios, and the histogram quantiles describe the whole process lifetime. Per-series deltas or rates (streamstats/delta by series, with reset handling) are needed before aggregating.

The internal_rej arm keeps only error_type apiserver_internal_error. Webhook timeouts and call failures are labelled calling_webhook_error, so the 'apiserver gave up waiting' critical tier (internal_rej>=3) will not fire on timeouts.

The cimSpl and the SPL tstats join query Application_State.app/.info/.state with nodename=Application_State. The deprecated Application State model's root dataset is All_Application_State and has no app, info or state fields, so cim_app_state is always null. like() inside a tstats WHERE clause may also be rejected.

The SPL uses an event search (search index=k8s_metrics ... __name__) while the Kubernetes guide queries k8s_metrics with mstats. If the splunk_hec exporter writes these Prometheus series to a metrics index, the event search returns nothing. Confirm the index type and the metric-name field before trusting the search.

summary: The detection idea (webhook latency share of apiserver wall time, plus 429/504 shedding) is well motivated, but the SPL cannot run as written (non-streaming commands inside multisearch), treats cumulative Prometheus counters as per-window values, misreads the webhook rejection error_type, and leans on a deprecated CIM model whose fields it invents. The prose also carries a second, generic Step 1-5 block that contradicts the first.
